articles.title: Kill-Chain Canaries: Stage-Level Tracking of Prompt Injection Across Attack Surfaces and Five Production LLMs
articles.summary: The paper introduces a kill-chain canary method to track how prompt-injection payloads move through multi-agent LLM systems across stages from exposure to execution. Across 950 runs involving five production LLMs, six attack surfaces, and five defense conditions, results varied significantly by model and channel, with Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 executing none of their reported text-surface attacks while GPT-4o-mini executed 53%. The study also found that some defenses failed when attacks moved through uninspected channels or different content formats.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a technical research update rather than a direct investment catalyst, but it highlights a key enterprise AI adoption constraint: securing agentic systems that read documents, web pages, tool outputs, and shared memory. The findings suggest model choice, workflow design, and channel-specific defenses may become important differentiators as companies move from basic chatbots to production multi-agent AI systems.

The model embeds each chunk with the full document in view and is trained to retrieve both answers and supporting evidence needed for verification.
